before.rock_grade: Easy 5th (low 5th, with a reported 5.4 crux move)
before.overview: Lundin Peak is a jagged, three-horned summit — the westernmost horn is the true summit — on the ridge connecting Snoqualmie Mountain (6,278 ft) to Red Mountain, immediately north of Snoqualmie Pass in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. Formerly named 'Snoqualmie Little Sister,' it was renamed in 1931 to honor district forest ranger John Lundin. Short approaches from I-90 and a mix of scrambling/low-5th rock make it one of the most popular half-day alpine objectives near Seattle, but the summit block is genuinely technical: expect Class 4 and low-5th (5.0-5.4) climbing with real exposure on the final pitch, not a walk-up scramble.

before.best_season: Mid to late season (July-September) for water availability and less snow. Early season (May-June) offers better route definition with snow but requires avalanche understanding.

waypoints.name: Lake Serene Trailhead (Bridal Veil Falls TH, US-2 near Index, WA)
waypoints.note: Traverse starts 'at the lake' (Lake Serene basin) and climbs the skyline right-to-left, summiting North Peak first then continuing over Middle and Main.
waypoints.directions: Take US-2 to milepost 35.2 and turn south onto Mount Index Road, following it 0.3 miles to the Lake Serene trailhead, also signed for Bridal Veil Falls. The maintained Lake Serene Trail #1068 leaves from here. Expect to be starting by headlamp: parties commonly need 12 to 15 hours or more, and many bivy.

before.approach: Start at the Lake Serene Trailhead and follow Trail #1068 about 4 miles and 2,000 ft of gain to Lake Serene, then traverse talus and boulders around the west side of the lake to its south end. From there head east to a saddle and climb the ridge/gully system southwest of it toward Main Peak, the massif's highest and most technical summit (~5,502 ft). Expect roughly 5,500 ft of total elevation gain, thick brush low on the route, and sustained moderate rock climbing higher up; most parties plan for a 15+ hour car-to-car day or an overnight.
